title: A’s top prospect Leo De Vries to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery: Source
content:
Leo De Vries, the Athletics’ No. 1-ranked prospect, will undergo right shoulder surgery and miss the rest of the minor-league season as part of an eight-month recovery, according to a team source who spoke Tuesday on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly about an upcoming procedure.

De Vries, the key acquisition in the 2025 trade that sent closer Mason Miller to the San Diego Padres, has not played a game since mid-August, when he was ultimately placed on the 60-day injured list with a shoulder issue. The 19-year-old shortstop opened the season at Double-A Midland and finished with an .836 OPS on 13 home runs and 21 doubles in 93 games.

In Keith Law’s updated top-70 prospect rankings, De Vries ranked third, behind Seattle Mariners right-hander Kade Anderson and Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Jesús Made.

“De Vries and Made are both outstanding prospects, and I would be fine with putting De Vries at No. 2 over Made, given their different skill sets but similar superstar upsides,” Law wrote then.

Though currently a shortstop, De Vries is expected to transition to another position, likely third base. The Padres signed him out of the Dominican Republic for $4.2 million, the second consecutive big swing for San Diego after signing catcher Ethan Salas in 2023 for $5.6 million. Earlier this month, Salas made his big-league debut, becoming the youngest player to catch a major-league game since Iván Rodríguez in 1991.

After the signing, the Padres assigned De Vries to Single-A Lake Elsinore, a full-season affiliate. He posted an .803 OPS over 75 games at that level before appearing in the Arizona Fall League.

By the end of 2025, De Vries went from High A to Double A over the course of a full year, finishing with an .806 OPS across all three levels. He opened the 2026 campaign in Double A.

Before going down with a shoulder injury, De Vries appeared in the 2026 Futures Game, singling in his first at-bat before stealing second and third base. De Vries scored for the American League team as part of a 1-for-2 day in the annual prospect showcase.

— Keith Law contributed to this report.
